layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (e-FRRO portal)
layers.process: The entire area of Nagaland is a Protected Area (Third Schedule, Immigration and Foreigners Order 2025). Every foreigner needs a Protected Area Permit to enter or stay. The Ministry of Home Affairs withdrew the 2010 exemption for Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland with immediate effect on 17 December 2024. Apply online at indianfrro.gov.in (e-FRRO) or the Indian Visa Su-Swagatam app; permits are electronic only. Indian missions advise getting approval 30 days ahead if applying with the visa, or applying to the FRRO at least 15 days ahead if already in India. Citizens of Afghanistan, China or Pakistan, and people of origin there, need the central government's prior approval.

layers.authority: Foreigners Registration Officer of the state or district
layers.process: Every foreigner visiting Manipur, Mizoram or Nagaland must register with the state or district Foreigners Registration Officer within 24 hours of arrival (MHA letter of 17 December 2024).

items.text: Nagaland has total prohibition under the Nagaland Liquor Total Prohibition Act 1989. The state Excise and Prohibition Department's main work is enforcing it, by controlling the possession, sale, consumption, manufacture and transport of liquor. Liquor for military and paramilitary units comes in separately, through canteen stores and bonded warehouses at Dimapur.

laws.rule: Nagaland bans possessing, selling, drinking, making and bringing in liquor under the Nagaland Liquor Total Prohibition Act 1989. Bringing in or selling liquor: 6 months to 3 years and a fine for a first offence (s 44). Drinking in public: up to 6 months and/or INR 2,000 (s 54).
